subject.title: Feature: durable natural-language rule learning + explicit multi-mention reply semantics

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class durable conversational rule-governance layer and default multi-bot mention semantics, or keep this split across memory plugins and channel-specific fixes?
rationale: The request changes persisted memory authority, workspace-file precedence, conflict handling, likely setting or command surface, and channel delivery semantics, so automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Keep As Design Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define rule authority, storage, conflict precedence, and cross-channel mention semantics before implementation.

options.title: Split The Work
options.body: Use narrower Feishu issues and PRs for message-loss fixes, and track durable memory governance separately only if maintainers want the rule layer.

options.title: Route Through Plugin/API Design
options.body: Require the durable rule-learning capability to prove it cannot be built through memory or plugin APIs before adding core rule-layer surface.

recommendation.title: Keep As Design Tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define rule authority, storage, conflict precedence, and cross-channel mention semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest current-main and recent-history signal across the memory prompt, memory-core, and Feishu mention paths inspected.
